topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session, connects it to prior histopathology practicals, and outlines the learning outcomes on cancer genetics and cellular transformation.

topics.label: Tumor viruses and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the historical role of tumor viruses in revealing cellular proto-oncogenes and describe the experimental assays used to demonstrate oncogenic transformation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the functional classification of cancer-driving mutations and illustrate how alterations in genes like Rb and p53 perturb cell cycle checkpoints through differing allele dosage effects.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how distinct defects in DNA repair pathways, replication fidelity, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how the stepwise accumulation of somatic and inherited mutations drives tumor progression and cancer susceptibility.

topics.label: Conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation, provides recommended reading, and previews the next lecture.
